summary: A design meets the trusted statement exactly when, for every width N with 1 ≤ N < 2^31, it has all of the properties below. Lean checks that, together, they say exactly what the statement says, nothing less and nothing more (the theorem statement_iff_properties).

properties.name: PARAMS_IN_RANGE
properties.text: The statement covers every width N with 1 ≤ N < 2^31 at once (the module's parameter is an int, which holds no larger value): one proof works for all of them, not just for the width the design is scored at (N = 16). Every property below must hold at each width.

properties.name: INTERFACE
properties.text: The module has exactly the input ports a and b (N bits each) and cin (1 bit) and exactly the output ports s (N bits) and cout (1 bit), with these widths, in this order. Nothing is missing and nothing is extra: an extra input could serve as a hidden mode pin, and the checker and the scoring tools drive and read the design by these names and widths.

properties.name: UNCLOCKED
properties.text: No process of the design runs at a clock edge: no always_ff, no always @(posedge …), no asynchronous-reset block; only continuous assignments and always_comb blocks. The task is combinational, so it never needs one. The rule closes a gap between Lean's model of SystemVerilog, which the proof is about, and real tools: the model runs every clocked block once per cycle whatever its clock does, so a design that registers correct outputs on a clock nothing drives would look right there, while a simulator sees a clock that never ticks and synthesis removes the registers.

properties.name: LOOP_FREE
properties.text: The design has no combinational loop: written as continuous assignments (each always_comb block becomes one), its processes can be ranked so that each reads only what lower-ranked ones write. A latch (an always_comb block that keeps a value on some path) is refused with it. Lean's model starts every signal at x and settles, so it would read a loop at one state, while a circuit powers up in any 0/1 state the loop can hold and keeps it; the rule removes that question instead of answering it. The ranking is of processes, not bits, so a process that reads a part of a signal it writes itself is refused too, even when no bit depends on itself: write such bits as separate assignments.

properties.name: TERMINATES
properties.text: Whatever order the simulator picks for processes that are ready at the same moment (the schedule), and whatever values the inputs take, simulating the design completes: every cycle settles. A combinational loop that oscillates fails this, and so does a design the tools could not read. It is also what gives the next property its teeth: that one is about completed runs, and a design with no completed run would satisfy it without computing anything.

properties.name: COMPUTES_SUM
properties.text: In every cycle in which the inputs a, b and cin are driven with known 0/1 values, the outputs settle to the sum: with t = a + b + cin taken as whole numbers, s = t mod 2^N (the low N bits) and cout = t div 2^N (the carry out, 0 or 1). So {cout, s} is the full (N+1)-bit sum and nothing is lost. The outputs must be fully known 0/1 values in every cycle of every run, whatever the earlier cycles were, so they cannot depend on history.

definitions.name: Statement
definitions.text: The trusted challenge statement that these properties restate, part by part.

definitions.name: task
definitions.text: The task as data: the parameter range, the ports at each parameter value, and the function the outputs must compute.

definitions.name: CombTask.SatisfiedAt
definitions.text: The trusted form of a combinational statement at one parameter value: the interface, then no clock and termination, then the function.

definitions.name: inputPorts
definitions.text: The design's input ports, each with its declared width, in declaration order.

definitions.name: outputPorts
definitions.text: The design's output ports, each with its declared width, in declaration order.

definitions.name: HoldAll
definitions.text: HoldAll st ports values: in the state st, every listed port holds its value as a known bit vector (no x, no z) of exactly the port's width.

definitions.name: ⊨₂
definitions.text: d ⊨₂ P: in every completed run of the design d, under every schedule and every stimulus, the stimulus and the trace satisfy P.

definitions.name: spec2
definitions.text: Turns a property of a stimulus (one input entry per cycle) and a trace (one snapshot of every signal per cycle) into the form ⊨₂ takes.

definitions.name: Runs2
definitions.text: Runs2 d σ stim tr: simulating d under the schedule σ on the stimulus stim completes, with the trace tr.

definitions.name: ScheduleOracle
definitions.text: A legal schedule: the order in which the simulator runs the processes that are ready at the same moment. The statement quantifies over all of them.

definitions.name: Process2.isEdgePhase
definitions.text: True for the processes that run at the clock edge: always_ff, always @(posedge …) and asynchronous-reset blocks.
